slides.texte_overlay:
How to turn your bedroom
into a place you truly rest
Keep work out of the bedroom. No laptop on the bed, no desk facing your pillow. Your brain should link this room with rest, not with emails.
Make it dark and cool. Thick curtains and a slightly cold room help you fall asleep faster and wake up less during the night.
Clear the floor and the surfaces. Clothes on chairs and piles of things keep your mind busy. A tidy room helps your thoughts slow down.
Invest in good bedding. A solid mattress, a comfortable pillow, clean sheets every week. You spend a third of your life there.
Before: I scrolled in bed until midnight. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science before sleep, and I fall asleep calmer.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: I scrolled in bed until midnight. After: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. I fall asleep calmer.

slides.texte_overlay: Use warm, low light in the evening. A small lamp instead of the ceiling light tells your body the day is ending.
Charge your phone outside the room. Use a simple alarm clock. Your nights become deeper and your mornings much calmer.
